correctness.rationale: The brush is one false-twin class, so at least q-1 brush leaves are mandatory. At that lower-bound size, the omitted brush leaf and p_1 both have all distances equal to two, so the set cannot resolve. The full brush resolves every handle vertex by its unique constant distance multiset. For size-q candidates with one omitted brush leaf, p_0 fails, while every p_j with j>=1 succeeds because q-1>=2 makes the repeated distance value recoverable and the only possible brush collision reduces to the impossible equation j+1=|j-1|. A direct exhaustive verifier checks all subsets for 35 parameter pairs.

value.rationale: Brooms are a standard and natural tree family with one large symmetric leaf class and an arbitrarily long handle. The theorem explains a sharp one-unit failure of the obvious twin lower bound, completely classifies all optimal resolving sets, and gives their exact count. This is a structural infinite-family result in a parameter for which the foundational tree literature is concentrated on paths and highly regular rooted trees.
